description: Three random control voltages that change together on a clock, each with its own depth and its own centre

params.text: Sets how far the first random voltage swings either side of its centre, from nothing at the bottom to 5V at the top
Sets how far the second random voltage swings either side of its centre, from nothing at the bottom to 5V at the top
Sets how far the third random voltage swings either side of its centre, from nothing at the bottom to 5V at the top
Chooses whether the outputs glide from one random value to the next across the gap between clocks, or jump straight to it and hold
Draws a fresh set of random values at once, without waiting for a clock

inputs.text: A rising edge above 1V draws a fresh set of random values; the measured time between edges also sets how long the smooth glide takes

outputs.text: The first random voltage, its swing set by POT1 and its centre by the menu offset
The second random voltage, its swing set by POT2 and its centre by the menu offset
The third random voltage, its swing set by POT3 and its centre by the menu offset

notes: With nothing patched into the clock jack the module runs on its own clock, at a rate chosen in the menu
Each output's centre is shifted by an offset chosen in the menu, and the result is held between -10V and +10V
It is an adaptation of the open-source HAGIWO MOD1 hardware, whose jack wiring fixes F1 as the only input and F2, F3 and F4 as the three outputs
menu: Clock rate — sets the module's own clock rate, used only while the clock jack is unpatched, from 0.1Hz up to 3Hz
CV1 offset — shifts the first output's centre, from -5V to +5V
CV2 offset — shifts the second output's centre, from -5V to +5V
CV3 offset — shifts the third output's centre, from -5V to +5V

inputs.0: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only
